title: Revoke.cash
description:
Hey all, we're building free and open source tools to help you stay safe in web3! 👋


To use tokens in decentralised applications such as Uniswap you have to grant the application permission to spend tokens on your behalf - known as a token approval. Token approvals are an important part of using these apps, but can be dangerous if left unchecked.


Bugs can exists and exploits can happen even in established projects, and by granting token approvals you are potentially exposing your wallet to these exploits. To keep yourself safe from exploits it is a good practice to regularly inspect and revoke your approvals.


Revoke.cash comes in as a preventative tool to manage your token approvals and practice proper wallet hygiene. By regularly revoking active approvals you reduce the chances of becoming the victim of exploits.


In many cases, phishing websites try to make you sign an approval while they pretend to be an NFT mint or other legitimate use cases. When these phishing scams happen, it is recommended to use Revoke.cash to mitigate the damage, but it is even better to prevent the scam in the first place.


This is where the Revoke.cash Browser Extension comes in. The extension pops up whenever you are about to sign an approval and will inform you of the approval's details. This can help you prevent signing malicious approvals.

title: Encrypt the Mempool! Stopping Toxic MEV & Censorship
description:
TL;DR

Shutter Network is building a movement to "Encrypt the Mempool!" and eliminate toxic MEV (frontrunning, sandwich attacks) and real-time censorship. Our work includes fun awareness campaigns, educational programs for all levels, protocol research, and public advocacy. We are rallying the community to implement encrypted mempools in the Ethereum protocol, thus making Ethereum more fair, credibly neutral, and secure for all users.



Problem Statement


Ethereum’s public mempool is broken.


Every transaction is visible in the public mempool before execution, giving sophisticated bots and builders the opportunity to re-arrange and censor transactions. Toxic MEV (front-running and sandwich attacks) have “extracted” billions of dollars from Ethereum users, degrades user experience, and prevents institutional adoption. Furthermore, real-time censorship runs contrary to user expectations and our core values of credible neutrality, permissionlessness and censorship resistance.


In recent years, private mempools have emerged as a temporary band-aid. They do protect users from toxic MEV (to some extent), but they introduce trusted third parties and promote builder centralization. Out-of-protocol solutions will never be enough.


Ethereum users face an impossible choice: become a victim of toxic MEV bots, or rely on unreliable intermediaries and betray their core values.


Solution


Encrypt the Mempool!


We believe the only way to solve this security problem is to “Encrypt the Mempool!” - thus allowing users to encrypt their transactions before sending them to the public mempool and then decrypt them after they have been ordered in the block.


We recognize that there are many ways to encrypt the mempool. We do not focus on one EIP, encryption standard, or technology. Instead, we work with a broad range of ecosystem actors (core developers, client teams, researchers, users, wallets, searchers, builders, and more) to promote deep understanding of the issues and work together to identify a solution which meets our shared needs. We do so with fun awareness campaigns, educational programs for all levels, protocol research, and public advocacy.


1. Security Awareness & Education 


We have built a massive repository of educational content to help ecosystem actors understand the Ethereum transaction supply chain, the problems of toxic MEV and real-time censorship, the dangers of centralization, and the robust protection offered by an encrypted public mempool. This includes:

  • Tech Deep Dives: Analyzing the "Holy Trinity of Censorship Resistance" and how encryption completes the Ethereum roadmap.
  • Debunking Myths: Clarifying misconceptions around latency and the technical limitations of encrypted mempools.
  • Cross-Platform Outreach: Extensive articles on CoinTelegraph, Coingecko, and CryptoNews, alongside a dedicated technical blog and podcast series.


Note: Full list of articles at the end of the description.


2. Security Advocacy


We have been (and still are!) on the front lines, advocating for an encrypted public mempool. We facilitate community calls, publish technical threads, host on-site workshops, lead working groups, and speak regularly at both leading and local conferences - from EthCC to EthTblisi. 


We published EIP-8105 (Universal Enshrined Encrypted Mempool), which sparked widespread discussions and innovations regarding encrypted public mempools. However, (as mentioned above) we are not partisans in favor of only one EIP or one approach. After LUCID was published, we withdrew EIP-8105 as a headliner candidate for Hegota and supported LUCID instead - working on a unified proposal with the best parts of each design. Now we are working with builders, wallets, Flashbots and others to further improve the design - and ensure it is ready for inclusion in I* Hardfork. 


Impact


In the past two years, our movement to “Encrypt the Mempool!” has challenged the status quo band-aid “solution” provided by private mempool, provided a rallying point for those seeking a real solution, and driven the discussion/innovation of encrypted mempool EIPs:

  • Built early awareness and support for an encrypted mempool EIP
  • Coverage on Cointelegraph, EthDaily, Ready for Merge, Etherworld, Daily Gwei, Ethereal News, Blockchain Socialist, and others
  • Event presentation and activation: EthCC, EthTbilisi, EthCC blue man activation and “Encrypt the Mempool!” button distribution
  • Dedicated EIP webpage, FAQ explainer for community
  • Regular content creation including educational threads, memes, 2 MEV explainer videos, and the “Voices from the Mempool” video series
  • Improved community understanding of encrypted mempools and how they complement ePBS and FOCIL for greater censorship resistance through regularly published news articles, podcasts, educational blog posts.
  • Built stakeholder relationships to support EIP implementation
  • Enlisted five decryptors for LUCID EIP: Enclave, Space Computer, Lit Protocol, Fairblock, Nillion
  • Outreach to key stakeholders for EIP feedback and production of FAQs to aid dev decision making: Clients, core devs, wallets, block builders
  • Launch of business/marcoms bi-weekly working group
  • Establish on-going relationships with media/community stakeholders for EM publicity: Ethdaily, Book of Ethereum, Cointelegraph, and others
  • Demonstrated encrypted mempools in production-like and live environments, while advancing encrypted mempool research
  • Live encrypted mempool on Gnosis Chain processed thousands of encrypted transactions with support from Nethermind and Erigon validators, proving the model works in production.
  • Launched encrypted mempool out-of-protocol POC on Primev; with live implementation in progress
  • Shutterized Beacon Chain research demonstrated how encrypted ordering can integrate safely with Ethereum consensus.
  • Deployment on the Sepholia OP Stack testnet validated encrypted flows in an L2 environment.
  • A previously published long-term roadmap, created with partners including Gnosis, Nethermind, Chainbound, and MEV Blocker, outlined the path for bringing encrypted mempools to Ethereum.
  • Contributed research on key open problems, including anti-collusion and the free option problem.


Use of Funds


Funding will be used to scale our education and advocacy efforts:


  • Encrypt the Mempool! Movement Content Production (<$10k): Producing of awareness and educational content for the Ethereum community and technical explainers and FAQs for core devs (covering range of formats video, images, threads, articles)
  • Community Advocacy and Events ($10k–$25k): Leading Encrypt the Mempool! working group for encrypted mempool publicity and outreach. Media outreach and coverage. Tx supply chain outreach and advocacy: wallets, clients, core devs, builders. Organizing workshops and technical sessions at major Ethereum conferences to rally developer support for encrypted mempools.
  • Research & Feedback Loops ($25k–$50k): Building an MEV simulator. Conducting surveys and gathering technical feedback from wallets, searchers, builders, and other ecosystem actors. 
  • Audit & Readiness ($50k+): Working to develop SDKs for easy wallet integration, efficient backrunning & rebase strategies for users, and efficient execution infrastructure for builders. Securing external security reviews for the proposed protocol changes to ensure they meet the rigorous safety standards required for a mainnet upgrade.

title: Protocol Guild
description:
Protocol Guild is the leading independent funding org for ~190 Ethereum core protocol contributors.


  • this includes client implementors (Besu, Erigon, EthereumJS, Geth, Grandine, Lighthouse, Lodestar, Nethermind, Nimbus, Prysm, Reth, Teku.), research, and support for network upgrades (ie. coordination, testing and devops).
  • Donations vest over 4 years directly to a split, which provides long-term incentives to steward the core protocol. Track all funding on our Dune dashboard.
  • The onchain member registry is curated by the membership and updated each quarter. Peer members doing the work are in the best position to make these assessments according to our eligibility framework.


We fund the people who scale the L1, Scale L2s (blobs) and improve interop UX. Some other work includes:


  • Scaling L1 via higher gas limits
  • Scaling L2s via more blobs
  • PoS evolutions including proposer build separation, LMD-GHOST confirmation rules and single slot finality
  • EVM and execution layer improvements: gas repricing, better UX for smart contract devs, state expiry
  • Cryptoeconomic research: multidimensional EIP-1559, POS timing games, prover incentives
  • Zero-knowledge proofs and cryptography research: post quantum, advancements to elliptic curve cryptography


All this work - foundational shared resources - is of extreme importance to the long-term success of Ethereum’s ecosystem, and yet funding for this work has historically come from a select number of entities, which only provide a fraction of the financial incentives compared to other available work (apps, L2s etc.), on a risk-adjusted basis. Our Sept 2025 report (Compensation Insights for Ethereum Core Developers) surfaced the fact that core devs pass up 50% of their market value do values-aligned work.


The Guild was created to serve as a counterbalance to this by giving core protocol contributors exposure to the broader ecosystem through things like the 1% Token Pledge. Overall, the Protocol Guild aims to secure the future of Ethereum, by enabling a highly efficient way for its ecosystem and community to sustainably fund core protocol development, while rebalancing incentives for core protocol contributors.


Just as the Ethereum distributed system takes inputs from many actors to produce a unified global state, the production of the underlying software combines efforts from many contributors. There is no single entity which maintains and evolves the protocol on their own.


Protocol Guild reproduces the qualities inherent to the production of a software commons as a funding stream: comprehensively curated, long-term oriented, and equitably distributed. With this tool, the ecosystem can now share the collective responsibility of funding core protocol stewardship.

title: rotki
description:
rotki is a fully opensource (AGPL) portfolio tracking, accounting & management app that puts users first. Unlike most financial apps, rotki never extracts your data, never locks you into someone else’s system, and never monetizes your privacy. It’s local-first software: your entire financial history lives on your machine, under your control.


In a world where most crypto apps are cloud-based and data-hungry, rotki is different. It’s an aligned app, built to serve its users, not exploit them.


Why rotki matters

Crypto is spread across centralized exchanges, multiple chains, and countless protocols. The result: a chaotic mess of wallets, trades, and balances. rotki brings clarity and control:


  • Unified portfolio view across exchanges, blockchains, and DeFi protocols.
  • Historical insight into your entire crypto journey: profits, losses, and positions.
  • Accounting & reporting tools that help you share results with an accountant without ever giving up your private data.
  • Privacy by design: no trackers, no hidden APIs, no accounts in someone else’s database.


How rotki improves Ethereum security

Every centralized portfolio tracker and tax tool is an attack surface. They collect wallet addresses, exchange API keys, full transaction histories, and net worth data into centralized databases. When these services get breached,and they do as we unfortunately keep seeing, attackers get a ready-made target list: who holds what, where, and how much. This is the reconnaissance phase of phishing, SIM-swap, and wrench attacks, handed over voluntarily by users who just wanted to track their portfolio. Today in France there is a crypto-related kidnapping every 2 days!!!! rotki eliminates this entire class of vulnerability by design:


  • No centralized honeypot. User data is encrypted and stored locally. There is no database of high-value wallets, api keys or history to exfiltrate. A breach of rotki's servers cannot compromise user financial data. We don't have them.
  • Open-source verifiability. Unlike closed-source competitors, rotki's codebase is fully auditable. Users and security researchers can verify there is no data exfiltration, no hidden telemetry, and no supply chain risk from opaque dependencies. This is trustless verification applied to financial tooling.
  • Privacy by design. No trackers, no hidden APIs, no accounts in someone else's database.


rotki proves that the crypto industry's unfortunately default pattern "give us all your data and trust us" is a choice, not a technical necessity.


Advocating for data sovereignty across Ethereum


Beyond the software itself, rotki's founder Lefteris Karapetsas actively uses his platform (~80k followers on X alone) to advocate for data sovereignty, local-first architecture, and privacy-preserving design across the Ethereum ecosystem. This includes raising awareness about the risks of centralized data collection in crypto tooling, the problem of centralized indexer dependencies (where even public blockchain data becomes gated by private companies), and the broader case that Ethereum's security depends not just on protocol hardening but on how users interact with the ecosystem day-to-day. rotki isn't just building an alternative it's making the case, publicly and consistently, that the Ethereum community deserves better than surveillance by default financial tools.


Where we’re going


rotki is already the most advanced local-first portfolio manager, but the vision is much bigger:

  • More supported protocols, chains, and integrations.
  • Smarter search, filtering, and analytics.
  • Portfolio management features that let users act, not just observe.
  • Continued innovation around privacy-preserving, user-aligned financial tools.


Why support matters


Because rotki refuses to monetize users through ads, lock-ins, or surveillance, we rely on community funding to keep the project alive. Donations directly support development, maintenance, and new features ensuring rotki remains independent, transparent, and aligned with its users.


By supporting rotki, you’re not just funding one app. You’re helping prove that aligned apps can survive and thrive: software that empowers people without exploiting them.


Donate today and help us build a healthier digital future for finance.

ETH.LIMO is a free and public ENS gateway that enables users to access Ethereum-native dApps and content. We’ve dedicated efforts to enhance the performance and reliability of our service, incorporating new features based on valuable feedback from the community. The eth.limo gateway is the default resolver for app.ens.domains and numerous other ENS projects. The ENS ecosystem and community operates best when all projects align and synergize their respective strengths. The eth.limo project extends broad name resolution for ENS, allowing builders to focus on their work and develop a user base. This positive feedback loop benefits both builders and the eth.limo gateway, driving increased traffic and engagement.


The LIMO project is organized around the following founding principles:

  1. Operate ETH.LIMO (gateway, DoH resolver, DNS resolver) as a public good.
  2. Provide support and technical guidance for builders and users.
  3. Work towards building a truly decentralized ENS/IPFS gateway service and global CDN..
  4. Develop and support DNS standards for ENS integrations.
  5. A commitment to open source software and the advancement of web3 through education, best practices, evangelism, and public accessibility.
  6. Ecosystem alignment to better collaborate and serve innovative projects.


Past experience working on ENS:

Since September 2021, we have been responsible for the maintenance, operation, and ongoing development of the eth.limo gateway.

We’ve dedicated efforts to enhance the performance and reliability of our service, incorporating new features based on valuable feedback from the community.

  • CCIP-read support: This has been enabled for the eth.limo resolver since July 2022. The current implementation leverages ethers.js to automatically query resolver contracts for CCIP gateways (if configured) and perform off-chain retrieval of the ENS record contenthash (https://offchainexample.eth.limo)
  • Automated, on-demand certificates for ENS subdomains
  • IPFS peering with all major content providers (Fleek, Web3 Storage, Cloudflare, etc…).
  • Accelerated DHT (Distributed Hash Table) support for IPFS. This results in faster retrieval times and a better user experience.
  • DNS over HTTPS (DoH) resolver. We now offer an easy to use DNS resolver for ENS domains. The DoH resolver can be integrated with applications for native ENS resolution, or even your browser! We feature both JSON and DNS wire format responses with DNSLink support.
  • Support for Swarm and Arweave Contenthashes
  • Support for Emoji and Unicode Domains
  • .art name resolution support
  • Reduced caching TTLs and synchronous cache expiry
  • General performance/stability/availability/security improvements


☑️LIMO takes public gateway services a step further by enforcing strong privacy guarantees such as never logging IP addresses or engaging in TCP fingerprinting. Limo now actively blocks FLoC (Federated Learning of Cohorts). This is a Google developed algorithm that tracks and correlates users based on their browsing history. FLoC enables advanced fingerprinting capabilities and greatly undermines online privacy and anonymity.


Running a Local Gateway - Your dWeb Swiss Army Knife


We've heard your feedback loud and clear! Now you can run a complete lightweight ENS gateway stack locally on your machine or even provide it as a service to your home or work network(s). This solution allows you to natively resolve ENS domains and dWebsite content without the need for third-party gateways.


This local stack has full feature parity with the public eth.limo service with the added benefits of trustless protocol interaction and complete customization.


Run your own private gateway that puts you in full control. Choose your own RPC provider or use a VPN/Tor for additional privacy. Each storage protocol uses its own light client for content verification, ensuring the integrity of the data you retrieve.

title: Dappnode
description:
Dappnode is a free and open source platform that allows anyone to easily deploy and run decentralized applications (DApps) and validators. By donating to Dappnode, you are supporting the development of a better user experience for the web3 ecosystem and helping to decentralize networks.


The dappnode software is completely free, and more than 4000 validators in Ethereum use it to maintain their nodes running and up-to-date. Dappnode doesn't, and can't, charge anything for it because it's built with self-sovereignty and privacy by design.


Currently, our focus is in becoming a public good beyond web3, allowing activists, journalists, and of course regular citizens to host their own privacy-enhancing, self-sovereign infrastructure like local-AI models, VPNs and others.


Your donations will directly impact the continued development and improvement of Dappnode, allowing us to create new features and enhancements that make it easier for users to access and use DApps. This in turn will help to further decentralize the Ethereum network and promote the use of decentralized technologies.

title: EVMcrispr
description:
EVMcrispr is an open-source toolkit for composing, simulating, and executing complex blockchain transactions safely.


Write human-readable scripts that batch multiple operations into single transactions, simulate them on chain forks, and verify outcomes with assertions, all before touching real funds.


What you can do with EVMcrispr:

  • Simulate before you execute. Fork any EVM chain (Ethereum, Arbitrum, Optimism, Base, Polygon, Gnosis, and more), run your transactions in a sandbox, manipulate state, and assert expected outcomes.
  • Batch complex operations. Combine token approvals, swaps, governance votes, treasury movements, and contract deployments into single atomic transactions.
  • Interact with any smart contract. Call any function on any contract with automatic ABI resolution, proxy detection, and type checking.
  • Manage DAOs. Full Aragon DAO support: install apps, manage permissions, create tokens, and execute governance proposals.
  • Work with on-chain and off-chain data. Read contract state, resolve ENS names, fetch HTTP APIs, parse JSON, and use the results in your scripts.
  • Automate with logic. Variables, conditionals (if/else), loops (for, while), user-defined functions, array operations, and string manipulation.
  • Integrate with AI. An MCP server and CLI enable AI agents to compose and execute blockchain transactions.


Proven in production: EVMcrispr has been adopted by a wide range of DAOs and decentralized organizations to handle governance, treasury operations, and protocol upgrades. Projects like Curve, Aragon, NFTX, 1Hive, Giveth, TECommons, BrightID, Agave, and DAppNode have relied on it to compose and execute complex on-chain votes, batching permission changes, token mints, funding allocations, contract upgrades, and even DAO chain migrations, into single, auditable transactions. For many of these communities, EVMcrispr became the standard way to safely prepare and simulate important proposals before they go to a vote, reducing the risk of costly mistakes in high-stakes DAO operations.


Real-world impact: EVMcrispr was used to simulate and encode the transaction that activated TheDAO Security Fund, a single batched call that safely moved over $220M in ETH and DAO tokens to establish Ethereum's largest security initiative.


EVMcrispr is free, open source (AGPL-3.0), and available at evmcrispr.com.


What we'll do with the funding:

  • Under $5k: Cover ongoing maintenance, hosting, and infrastructure costs. Continue bug fixes and community support.
  • $5k–$10k: Fund development of new security-focused features: expanded simulation assertions and improved error reporting for safer transaction composition. Cover travel costs for in-person workshops (such as Barcelona and Cannes, March 2026).
  • $10k–$25k: All of the above, plus develop a comprehensive educational program: written tutorials, video walkthroughs, and workshop curriculum for teaching blockchain operations security using EVMcrispr. Expand simulation backend capabilities (such as cross-chain simulations).
  • $25k–$50k: All of the above, plus expand MCP capabilities with built-in security guidelines that leverage existing assertion mechanisms to enforce safer transaction composition. A dedicated development sprint to build advanced security features like transaction diff visualization. Expand the workshop program to multiple events.
  • $50k+: All of the above, plus launch a community solutions forum, a curated, searchable knowledge base where users can share and discover proven approaches to common blockchain operations challenges. Establish a regular workshop series across Ethereum events.
